message_1_subject: Synapse AI POC: sprint canvas + SDK/API routing commitments
message_1_body:
Hi Priya / Samir,

Thanks again for taking the call this morning — great conversation and clear product fit. Per our discussion, I pulled together a compact POC sprint canvas and a proposed integration route so we can kick off next week. High-level recap: 

- Success criteria (what Synapse will evaluate):
  * 90th percentile latency <= 120ms for single-turn generation at target QPS (100 rps).
  * End-to-end accuracy: generated outputs match gold prompts > 85% on the sample prompt set.
  * Stable streaming experience with reconnect/resume for sessions up to 2k tokens.

- Proposed scope (4-week sprint):
  1) Week 0: Kickoff, access & sample dataset ingestion.
  2) Week 1: SDK integration and auth (API keys + SSO test).
  3) Week 2: Streaming + tool-calling proof points (browser client + backend).
  4) Week 3: Load validation, acceptance run, and evaluation scoring.

- Ownership: 
  * Redwood: SDK deliverable, streaming endpoint, runbook for scaling. (Marcus owns runtime config.)
  * Synapse: sample prompts, acceptance test set, and security signoff. (Priya to coordinate).

Attachments: I've attached the sprint canvas (synapse-poc-sprint-canvas.pdf) and an initial API route matrix (api-route-matrix.csv).

Next steps / ask:
- Can you confirm the success criteria above or note any changes by EOD Tuesday?
- If those look good we'll schedule a 30-min kickoff for Wed to assign access and invite infra owners.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference

message_3_subject: Re: Synapse AI POC: streaming client + auth + route details
message_3_body:
Hi Priya / Samir — Karthik from the runtime team here. Short technical notes to address the asks: 

1) SDK + Auth
- We will provide a JS + Python SDK. Auth: API key for the POC + optional OAuth 2.0 client credentials for the staging VPC. Key rotation is supported; we can emit short-lived tokens via a token exchange endpoint.

2) Streaming behavior and KV cache on reconnect
- Streaming endpoint: wss://streaming.redwood.ai/v1/stream?sdk=js
- Reconnect policy: clients send session_id + last_seen_token_index. We rehydrate KV cache automatically for the session up to the last 8k tokens (beyond that we provide a partial cold-start).
- If session_id is missing on reconnect, we treat request as a new session (no KV resume). We'll include an example client that demonstrates resume and exponential backoff.

3) API routes and sample cURL (also in api-route-matrix.csv)
- POST /v1/generate (sync generation, accept streaming=false)
- POST /v1/stream (upgrade or websocket for streaming)
- POST /v1/tool/call (server-side tool invocation pattern; returns tool run id and status)

Sample cURL for sync generation:
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-large-v1","input":"Summarize the following...","max_tokens":256}'

4) Logs & retention (for Priya's security team)
- Audit logs: request metadata, auth id, and model version are written to our audit stream. Default retention for POC accounts is 90 days; can be extended for Dedicated/Private deployments. Logs are available via a signed S3 link or pushed to a customer-owned S3/GCS bucket.

I'll attach a minimal streaming client example in the shared Drive and link the example code in the follow-up. Marcus — can you confirm SLOs for token latency under the projected QPS?

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
